date.as_written: nabhorasābdhyaikamite śakebde saṃvatsare caiva parābhaākye ṛtau śarannāmni karāhvayetho sadosvije māsi ca somavāre || ādimāyāṃ tithau caiva site pakṣe ca vaidhṛtau

notes: Chronogram: nabhas 0, rasa 6, abdhi 4, eka 1. Read right to left this gives ŚS 1460 (c. 1538 CE), which matches the catalogue. The saṃvatsara is named Parābhava. In the southern 60-year cycle Parābhava falls in ŚS 1468 (1546/47), and ŚS 1460 would be Vilambin. Under northern Bārhaspatya reckoning the name may differ by a few years, so the year and the saṃvatsara do not fully agree. 'sadosvije' is probably a corruption of 'sad-āśvije' (Āśvina). 'karāhvaye 'tho' is taken as the nakṣatra Hasta. 'prayoga' may be a corruption of 'prayāge' (written at Prayāga), but this is uncertain. Both readings fit the anuṣṭubh metre. The scribe is identified in the quoted text only as the son of Jogadeva (reading of 'jo(ga)' uncertain). The name Rāmeśvarabhaṭṭa is the catalogue's tentative suggestion, perhaps from the omitted line 10, so it is not verified. Caritravardhana is the author of the commentary, not connected with this copy.
